assets.defect_engineered: the printed page reads as a square photo well above three tidy type lines, but the CONVERSION exposes something else: the picture frame's true bounds are PORTRAIT and inset under the type block (not the square it prints as), and the name / role / company lines that print as three separate lines actually sit in ONE continuous text story; on top of that the story readout can drop a run while keeping its line break so every offset past it runs short — none of which is visible on the printed page
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the badge printer's own conference-badge press PDF (flat, single record; to be converted to .indd and reverse-engineered into a fourteen-record data merge downstream).

Document: single badge, 4 x 3 inches LANDSCAPE (101.6 x 76.2 mm), fonts embedded, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed). This is the artwork the badge printer already runs a strip of; they want one page per person returned.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (four apparent zones):
- Top-left: a neat SQUARE PHOTO WELL, roughly 1.1 x 1.1 in, showing a placeholder head-and-shoulders portrait.
- To its right, a NAME line in a bold display face, large.
- Under the name, a ROLE line in a lighter sans, medium.
- Under the role, a COMPANY line ('Nimbadesk') in small caps, with a thin Signal Blue rule beneath it.
- A slim Signal Blue #2E6BE6 accent band down the left edge.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The picture frame is NOT the square it appears to be. Its true bounds are PORTRAIT (taller than wide, roughly 0.95 x 1.25 in) and INSET UNDER the type block, cropped by an overlapping shape so only a square window shows on the printed page. Any photo bound into the frame is placed to the portrait bounds, not the visible square, so plates cut to a square will sit wrong.
- The NAME line, the ROLE line and the COMPANY line are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame (three paragraph breaks inside one story), NOT three addressable frames. Fields must be placed by paragraph position inside the one story, not by frame.
- On conversion the story's text readout can OMIT a run (e.g. the company paragraph) while keeping its line break, so every character offset computed past the omission is short and a positionally-computed mapping lands its later placeholders in the wrong place — yet generate_indd_mapping_prompt still reports the mapping valid and prepare_indd_merge_template still reports success.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called; 300 DPI trim-only is the honest ceiling.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): PHOTO | NAME | ROLE | COMPANY

Colours: Paper #FFFFFF ground, Nimbus Ink #16233A name text, Slate #5B6B82 role text, Signal Blue #2E6BE6 left accent band and the rule under the company line, Mist #EEF2F8 photo-well backing.

assets.content:
NIMBADESK - LAUNCH COPY (approved, final for this quarter; we change pricing every quarter)

TAGLINE
Support desk, minus the drama.

VOICE
Direct, specific, understated. Numbers carry the argument and every claim states its period. We sell to the person who defends the line item to finance, so everything we show is real.

=== SELL SHEET 1 - UNIFIED QUEUE ===
Header: One queue. Clear ownership.
Advantage: Shared inboxes hide who owns what. Nimbadesk puts every request in one queue with a single owner, a status and an assignee, so nothing sits unclaimed.
Core bullets:
- One queue for email, chat and web requests
- Explicit owner and status on every ticket
- Saved views and search across the whole history
- Handoffs that keep the thread intact
CTA: See your queue in a 20-minute walkthrough.

=== SELL SHEET 2 - SLA & ROUTING ===
Header: Rules that route, targets that hold.
Advantage: Priorities and escalations run on rules you set, not on whoever happens to be watching. First-response and resolution targets are measured, not hoped for.
Core bullets:
- IF/THEN routing by priority, tag and queue
- First-response and resolution SLA targets with business hours
- Automatic escalation before a target is breached
- An escalations board that shows what is at risk
CTA: Set your first SLA in an afternoon.

=== SELL SHEET 3 - REPORTING FOR DIRECTORS ===
Header: Reporting a director can actually read.
Advantage: The numbers your finance director asks for, on one page, with the period stated. No dashboards nobody opens.
Core bullets:
- Open, resolved and median-response KPIs at a glance
- Volume and load by team and by agent
- CSAT trend with the comments behind it
- Every figure labelled with the window it covers
CTA: Get the launch reporting pack.

=== TIERS (per seat, monthly; final for this quarter) ===
Starter - $29/seat - up to 3 agents, one queue, email support
Team - $79/seat - RECOMMENDED - unlimited queues, SLA & routing, reporting, integrations
Scale - $249/seat - advanced routing, audit log, priority support, single sign-on
Enterprise - approx. $18,000/year annual - custom SSO, security review, dedicated success
(The middle tier, Team at $79, is the one we recommend and want to read as recommended.)

=== ROADMAP ===
Q1 - Launch, sign-ups open, integrations directory
Q2 - Custom SLA policies, satisfaction surveys
Q3 - Workflow automations, mobile app
Q4 - Analytics API, advanced permissions
